title: Time Complexity [Learn Basics, and then analyse in next Steps]
subStepTitle: Things to Know in C++/Java/Python or any language
subcategory: Things to Know in C++/Java/Python or any language
problemStatement: Estimate runtime and memory scaling to predict TLE / MLE before you code.
intuition: Drop constants and lower-order terms. ~1e8 ops/sec rule of thumb. O(n²) with n=1e5 → TLE. O(n²) int tables with n=1e4 → MLE risk. Recursion stack is not O(1).

approaches.title: Constraints → algorithm family
approaches.idea: Read limits first; pick a complexity budget; reject impossible families.
algorithm: Identify n, m, k from constraints.
Count nested loops / branching / heavy ops.
Compare to time/memory limits → TLE/MLE flags.
approaches.code:
# Feasibility sketch (typical single-test):
# n <= 20      → O(2^n * poly)
# n <= 400     → O(n^3) borderline
# n <= 5000    → O(n^2) usually OK
# n <= 1e5     → O(n log n) / O(n)
# n <= 1e12    → O(log n) / math

def looks_quadratic(a: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(a)
    best = 0
    for i in range(n):          # O(n^2) — TLE if n ~ 1e5
        for j in range(i, n):
            best = max(best, a[j])
    return best

specialTechnique.title: TLE / MLE / RE / WA
specialTechnique.body:
TLE — too slow (or constant too large).
MLE — too much memory.
RE — crash (OOB, div0, recursion depth).
WA — wrong answer.

Always separate:
• Time
• Auxiliary space
• Input space
• Recursion stack depth

commonMistakes: O(n²) DP for large n → MLE+TLE
patternRecognition: Read constraints before choosing the family.
n=1e5 ⇒ discard O(n²) unless asked for brute force first.
followUps: Why Python O(n log n) may TLE where C++ passes?
interviewInsight: Narrating complexity and TLE/MLE risk before coding is a strong SDE-2/3 signal.
